correctness.rationale: For all 3432 subsets of size seven, the standard exact graph-state amplitude trace proves a flat Schmidt spectrum controlled by binary cross-cut rank. Every cross-cut matrix splits into two explicit square incidence subblocks. Two independently constructed Fano representations with separate GF(2) Gaussian elimination implement complete enumeration and agree exactly on the histogram 100/980/1680/672 and the composition table. The direct adjacency algorithm also verifies the 21-edge canonical split rank four, exact entropy mean 5021/858, and 336 rank-seven cuts at each of 11 and 13 crossing edges. No infinite or larger-graph extrapolation is claimed.

The inspected public Heawood linear-arrangement theorem optimizes edge-boundary cardinalities and cutwidth, not binary cross-adjacency rank or quantum entanglement.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the smallest cubic incidence cage and a canonical 14-qubit stabilizer resource. The exact complete balanced-cut entanglement distribution is a natural finite invariant for which the general rank formula alone does not provide the evaluated answer. The 672 maximally entangled cuts and the exact 21-edge/4-ebit versus 11–13-edge/7-ebit inversion provide a substantive non-monotonic preparation-edge versus accessible-entanglement boundary, directly useful in comparing resource partitions. The contribution is an exact classification, not an arbitrary low-order correction, with the normal finite-graph scope honestly stated.
